questions.question: How can you avoid slowing down traffic when driving a large truck?

options.text: Pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy truck cannot keep up with other traffic, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: How should you park to leave safely and easily?

options.text: Park so you must back up to leave.
Park so you can pull forward to leave.
Park on the side of a roadway, not in a lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park so you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous. Park in a way that lets you pull forward to exit instead.

questions.question: When are you most likely to encounter strong winds?
questions.correctAnswerText: Coming out of tunnels.
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. This is especially a problem when exiting a tunnel.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air storage tanks?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They hold compressed air for the brakes.
They should be drained after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold the compressed air needed to operate the air brake system. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of tanks.

questions.question: What equipment must a truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.correctAnswerText: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: What should you do if your engine catches fire?

options.text: Open the hood as soon as possible.
Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine right away to stop the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless necessary.

questions.question: What is the best way to back up?

options.text: Use only the passenger's side mirror.
Turn toward the passenger's side whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper if possible.
questions.explanation: When backing, go slowly and use both side mirrors. Have someone help you watch the blind spots if possible. Agree on a signal for "stop" with your helper.

questions.question: When driving downhill, brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph below your safe speed.
questions.explanation: When going downhill, press the brake until you slow to 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: What should a driver do when pulled over on the side of the road?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What should you do when backing a truck?

options.text: Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Always use mirrors on both sides when backing. Have a helper watch your blind spots whenever possible.

questions.question: A cargo van with a heavy load will:

options.text: Be about the same height as when empty.
Be taller than when carrying a light load.
Be lower than when carrying a light load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be lower than when carrying a light load.
questions.explanation: Heavy loads push a vehicle down. A vehicle sits higher when empty or lightly loaded than when fully loaded. A vehicle that fits under an overpass when full may not fit when empty.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of drowsy driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Feeling hungry
questions.explanation: Signs of drowsy driving include frequent blinking, eyes closing or losing focus on their own, yawning a lot, and drifting between lanes. Drowsy driving is dangerous and must be avoided.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians cannot see you. Be ready for them to move into your path suddenly. A light horn tap or flashing lights may be safe to use while passing.

questions.question: A maximum safe speed sign means:

options.text: It is only a suggestion. Vehicles may drive faster than posted.
It only applies to vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds.
No vehicle should go faster than the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No vehicle should go faster than the posted speed.
questions.explanation: You must never drive faster than the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.

questions.question: The minimum tire tread depth for rear tires is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Check that front tires have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth in every main groove. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: When braking a vehicle with ABS, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way you would in any vehicle. Do not brake differently just because the vehicle has ABS.

questions.question: Looking ahead at the road helps you:

options.text: Plan how to avoid hazards before you reach them.
Stay focused, and is not a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to avoid hazards before you reach them.
questions.explanation: Always watch the road ahead for hazards. This gives you time to react before you encounter them.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you better control when braking.
Slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: If ABS is on only the tractor, only the trailer, or only one axle, you still have more braking control than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: Parking brakes should be:

options.text: Tested only after you have driven some distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tested before you drive.
questions.explanation: Test your parking brake as part of your pre-trip check before driving. If the parking brake does not hold, repair the vehicle before driving it.

questions.question: In bad weather, a driver of a double or triple should:

options.text: Lead the way for other drivers.
Drive on the shoulder of the road.
Drive carefully because these vehicles skid easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully because these vehicles skid easily.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, take extra care when driving doubles or triples. They are at high risk for skids, loss of traction, and rollovers.
